subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should OpenClaw own Herdr state reporting as a bundled plugin-gated TUI integration, as explicit core TUI behavior, or outside core?
rationale: The diff mixes a default-on bundled plugin with core env-triggered runtime behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or compatibility contract.

options.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
options.body: Keep the bundled plugin direction, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global disablement, denylist, allowlist, and per-plugin disablement.

options.title: Make It Core-Owned
options.body: Remove the no-op plugin wrapper and document the ambient `HERDR_PANE_ID` behavior as an explicit core TUI feature with matching live proof.

options.title: Move Outside Core
options.body: Pause or close the PR unless a generic missing TUI/plugin seam is identified, leaving Herdr-specific polling to ClawHub or an external integration.

recommendation.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Keep the bundled plugin direction, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global disablement, denylist, allowlist, and per-plugin disablement.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans plugin policy and TUI lifecycle, both areas with recent history from this owner candidate.
